Overhead Lines
Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: TL-033-r0a
Equipment: Medium-voltage overhead lines
Issued to: Distribution Companies
Status: Approved
Approval date: 12 February 2006
Procedure: Fitting the mid-span joint
Next review date: February 2011

sections_en.text: This document sets out the steps for fitting the mid-span joint on medium-voltage lines. It was prepared by the Minya Electricity Distribution Sector, Middle Egypt Electricity Distribution Company, and discussed, amended and approved by the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.

rows: Issue a work permit and a work order, with the workers on site carrying an occupational safety and health category card.
Fence off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs.
The occupational safety and health equipment must be used, taking care to wear the safety belt and fix it well to the tower, observing the appropriate clearance for freedom of movement.
Make sure both sources of supply are disconnected from the line to be worked on and that it is earthed from both sides, and earthed before and after the joint work area.
Make sure the tools used for making the joint are sound before starting work (rope, press, grips, ferrules, steel cutter, pulleys).
If there is an assistant below the tower, he must not stand directly below the tower, to avoid any tool falling on him.

Observe the correct technical specifications when making the joint, since it is exposed to tensile forces that may affect its strength and consequently expose personnel to the risk of conductors breaking and falling randomly.
Portable earth, voltage indicator.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety belt, etc.
Aluminium ferrules of different sizes.
Aluminium lugs of different sizes, copper lugs of different sizes in the case of copper wire.
Die set (of different sizes suitable for the lug cross-sectional area), ratchet.
Screwdriver set of different sizes, spanner set (open-end and ring), pliers for removing insulator accessories.
Clamps, grip, rope, a set of pulleys for pulling the conductors.
Press, steel cutter, threaded bolts with washers for fixing.
Adhesive tape, electrical grease, Vaseline, cleaning tools before compression (rags), cleaning material (caustic potash).

sections_en.text: Procedures to be Carried Out (Figure No. 1), carried out on the ground

rows: Fit the ends of the two conductor ends so that they are well stranded.
Clean the two ends and apply light Vaseline.
Use the Double Groove ferrule.
Insert the two conductor ends into the ferrule with 25 cm extra from each end.
Insert the clamping strip between the two conductors inside the ferrule by light tapping towards its end.
Compress using a hydraulic press at a rate of 6 consecutive compressions at equal distances.
Bend the two ends protruding from the ferrule for the two conductors and insert them into a cylindrical ferrule, then compress them as in the bridle joint.

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for fitting the mid-span joint on medium-voltage lines. It was prepared by the Minya Electricity Distribution Sector, Middle Egypt Electricity Distribution Company, and discussed, amended and approved by the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
Safety Precautions
Issue a work permit and a work order, with the workers on site carrying an occupational safety and health category card. | 
Fence off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs. | 
The occupational safety and health equipment must be used, taking care to wear the safety belt and fix it well to the tower, observing the appropriate clearance for freedom of movement. | 
Make sure both sources of supply are disconnected from the line to be worked on and that it is earthed from both sides, and earthed before and after the joint work area. | 
Make sure the tools used for making the joint are sound before starting work (rope, press, grips, ferrules, steel cutter, pulleys). | 
If there is an assistant below the tower, he must not stand directly below the tower, to avoid any tool falling on him. | 
Observe the correct technical specifications when making the joint, since it is exposed to tensile forces that may affect its strength and consequently expose personnel to the risk of conductors breaking and falling randomly. | 
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Portable earth, voltage indicator. | 
Occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety belt, etc. | 
Aluminium ferrules of different sizes. | 
Aluminium lugs of different sizes, copper lugs of different sizes in the case of copper wire. | 
Die set (of different sizes suitable for the lug cross-sectional area), ratchet. | 
Screwdriver set of different sizes, spanner set (open-end and ring), pliers for removing insulator accessories. | 
Clamps, grip, rope, a set of pulleys for pulling the conductors. | 
Press, steel cutter, threaded bolts with washers for fixing. | 
Adhesive tape, electrical grease, Vaseline, cleaning tools before compression (rags), cleaning material (caustic potash). | 
Procedures to be Carried Out (Figure No. 1), carried out on the ground
Fit the ends of the two conductor ends so that they are well stranded. | 1.
Clean the two ends and apply light Vaseline. | 2.
Use the Double Groove ferrule. | 3.
Insert the two conductor ends into the ferrule with 25 cm extra from each end. | 4.
Insert the clamping strip between the two conductors inside the ferrule by light tapping towards its end. | 5.
Compress using a hydraulic press at a rate of 6 consecutive compressions at equal distances. | 6.
Bend the two ends protruding from the ferrule for the two conductors and insert them into a cylindrical ferrule, then compress them as in the bridle joint. | 7.
